changed_by.title: chore: bring in the reference feature and the comment sweep

adam.assumes: Neon's HTTP driver sends every query through `neonConfig.fetchFunction`, which `src/db/client.ts` sets to `outboundFetch`. I read this from memory of the driver's source, not from the installed version.
adam.if_wrong: A query to a database that never answers would hang the page with no 5-second limit, and nothing would report that the limit is not applied.

adam.assumes: Vercel's Neon integration gives a preview's build the `DATABASE_URL` of that preview's own database branch, as the seed `ARCHITECTURE.md` says. I could not confirm this from Vercel's or Neon's documentation here.
adam.if_wrong: A pull request's build would run `src/db/migrate.mts` against production's database, so an unreviewed migration changes production's tables before anyone merges, and no check reports it.

lesson.summary: The first `ci` run after pull request #591 did what the change claimed: the pull request removed only a comment from `ci.yml`, the workflow still loaded and succeeded, and nothing needs doing.
lesson.detail: Pull request #591 changed one line of `factory/workflows/ci.yml`: it deleted the comment above the step "Start a retro when this job failed" in the `start-fix` job. It changed no step, condition or command there, so the facts list no changed step. Run 44962683434, on pull request #594, loaded the installed workflow and concluded with success: the `checks`, `e2e` and `review` jobs passed, and Adam and Ryan each completed (12 and 13 seconds, $0.52 and $0.51). The `merge` and `start-fix` jobs were skipped as written, so the step beneath the removed comment did not run; a removed comment gives it nothing new to prove. Adam's two assumptions on #591 concern the project template's Neon driver and Vercel's preview database, which no `ci` run in this repository exercises, so this run neither confirms nor refutes them.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run succeeded, and its two reviews cost $1.03 and 25 seconds of sessions as any review does.

lesson.saves: Nothing: there was no fault to prevent.
